title: Quarantine straggler stream frames to prevent client-visible glitches
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Summary: Several customers reported client-side partial or duplicated output after brief network blips when consuming Hosted SSE streams. Symptoms include: (1) clients receiving a short, duplicated tail frame that appears out of causal order; (2) incomplete final messages marked as finished despite missing final token(s); (3) downstream SDKs surfacing JSON parse errors when streamed deltas are stitched. Impact: Production customers with long-running sessions experienced downstream UX corruption (chat history gaps, duplicated assistant lines) and a major customer escalated to SE. Repro rate observed in telemetry is ~0.03% of streams but concentrated in sessions with >30s long-lived SSE connections and intermittent reconnects. Repro steps: 1) Open SSE stream to hosted API with streaming=true and keepalive interval 30s. 2) Simulate 150–500ms network blip and restore. 3) Observe client receives a short trailing event that contains a suffix token sequence that doesn't match server snapshot. Root cause hypothesis: race between session checkpoint flush and connection teardown: the runtime emits a final flush (checkpoint delta) to the stream writer while an edge proxy (ingress) closes the TCP connection mid-flush, which causes the writer to requeue/flush a truncated frame on the next session resume path. The resumed session's rehydration logic concatenates the truncated tail as if it were an independent micro-event, resulting in duplicated or malformed final tokens. Proposed fix: introduce a quarantine layer for "straggler frames" at the stream assembly boundary. Quarantine semantics: - Any frame that arrives after a connection TEARDOWN event but before session checkpoint is acknowledged will be held in a short-lived buffer (quarantine window) and validated against the authoritative session snapshot before being emitted to the client. - A checksum marker will be added to checkpoint boundaries so resumed sessions can deterministically detect and drop replayed truncated tail frames. - Add a circuit that fails open for low-latency SLO classes (tiered policy) if quarantine validation would otherwise exceed 10ms additional latency. Implementation plan: 1) Create quarantine buffer and checksum markers in runtime stream writer (runtime-1.22 branch). 2) Add validation step in resume/rehydration path to compare quarantine frames to authoritative snapshot. 3) Add observability: per-session quarantine_hits, quarantine_drops, quarantine_latency_ms, and example traces in tracing UI. 4) E2E tests with flaky network harness and unit tests for checksum correctness. Rollout plan: Canary on Hosted region us-west-2 (10% traffic) for 48h, then 50% for 24h, then 100% with rollback window. Backfill and compatibility: Resume heuristics will fall back to current behavior if checkpoint metadata missing; consult Dedicated/Private product teams to plan backport or configuration toggle for on-prem customers. Security & compliance: no plaintext customer data changes; checksum metadata is opaque. Required approvals: runtime-team, platform-proxy, QA. Links to artifacts and dashboards are below.

2026-03-06 - Design sync: Proposed quarantine buffer and checksum markers. Trade-off: adds up to 10ms extra validation latency; agreed to make policy tiered (canary only) and fail-open for low-latency traffic classes.

2026-03-08 - Review feedback: @eva-nguyen requested clearer operational metrics and a config flag. Added runtime flag --quarantine-window-ms and per-session histograms. Updated PR.
2026-03-09 - QA: Added flaky-network integration test; observed quarantine_drops for >1% of fuzzed sessions (expected). Tests passing locally. Preparing canary deployment manifest.

2026-03-11 - SE follow-up: Provided AcmeChat with a temporary mitigation (client-side stitch sanitizer) and a retroactive data fix for affected sessions. Customer confirmed reduced UX corruption after sanitizer deployment.
